answer: Each agent can escrow a stake that is slashed when independent audits find fabricated work or collusion; rewards accrue only after a delayed challenge window, so a new identity cannot instantly cash out. Auditors compare signed task histories for repeated patterns, using delta changes to flag copied behavior and an echo of prior submissions as evidence, not proof. A harbor of reputable peers can vouch for newcomers, but those peers also lose stake if their endorsements repeatedly lead to fraud. A sybil attacker must therefore fund many identities, wait, and risk losing capital.
